reason: The passage (Exodus 1:15-22) depicts Hebrew midwives (Shiphrah and Puah) who explicitly fear God (וַתִּירֶאן אֶת־ הָאֱלֹהִים - yirah et-Elohim). Their fear of Yahweh causes them to defy Pharaoh's command to kill Hebrew male infants, thereby preserving Hebrew lives. By choosing obedience to God over obedience to the earthly ruler, they demonstrate that allegiance to Yahweh is their primary commitment. God explicitly rewards their fear and faithfulness (וַיֵּיטֶב אֱלֹהִים לַֽמְיַלְּדֹת), and the Hebrew people multiply and strengthen, reinforcing their identity as those under God's protection and covenant. The narrative structure supports that being followers of Yahweh is indeed their 'first and foremost' characteristic, as it supersedes even fear of the pharaoh.
